question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom below.
“Cost an arm and a leg”

(ASI Steno and Head Constable Ministerial Group C)
options: to be very expensive
to be in a comfortable situation
to be in an uncomfortable situation
to be quite inexpensive
solution:
The correct answer is: to be very expensive

Explanation:
"Cost an arm and a leg" - "बहुत महंगा होना"
This idiom is used to describe something that is extremely expensive, implying that the price is so high it feels like losing a limb.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originated in mid-20th century America, where losing an arm or a leg was considered a devastating loss. Comparing the cost of something to such a loss emphasizes how exorbitant the price is.

Example:
"Buying a luxury car can cost an arm and a leg."
"लक्ज़री कार खरीदना बहुत महंगा पड़ सकता है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "cost an arm and a leg" is "to be very expensive" because it conveys the idea of something being excessively costly. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.Hegoes hard withone and all.
(Stenographer Grade C and D Examination 2024)
options: To be unreliable
To be difficult
To be busy over trifles
To remain neutral
solution:
The correct answer is: To be difficult

Explanation:
"Goes hard with" - "किसी के लिए मुश्किल होना"
The idiom "goes hard with" means something is difficult or harsh for someone. In the given sentence, it implies that the situation is tough or challenging for everyone involved.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the idea of something being physically or emotionally hard (difficult) to endure. Over time, it evolved into a figurative expression to describe challenging circumstances.

Example:
"The new policy goes hard with small business owners."
"नई नीति छोटे व्यवसायियों के लिए मुश्किल साबित हो रही है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "goes hard with" is "to be difficult" because it conveys the idea of hardship or struggle. The other options ("to be unreliable," "to be busy over trifles," "to remain neutral") do not match the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
In the following questions a statement has been given with highlighted text. Select the options that can replace the text with correct idiom or phrase.
Reginald betrayed his closest friend. It was big shock for all.
(CHSL 2021 Tier I)
options: A black sheep
Stab someone in the back
Every cloud has a silver lining
Looking to your laurels
solution:
The correct answer is: Stab someone in the back 

Explanation:
The idiom "stab someone in the back" means to betray someone, especially when they trust you. Since the statement describes Reginald betraying his closest friend, this idiom fits perfectly.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

[A black sheep] – कुल का कलंक – A person who is considered a disgrace or an embarrassment to their family or group.
Example: "He was the black sheep of the family because he never followed traditions."

[Stab someone in the back] – पीठ में छुरा घोंपना – To betray someone who trusts you.
Example: "She pretended to be my friend but later stabbed me in the back by stealing my promotion."

[Every cloud has a silver lining] – हर मुसीबत में एक अवसर छुपा होता है – There is something good in every bad situation.
Example: "I lost my job, but every cloud has a silver lining—now I can start my own business."

[Looking to your laurels] – अतीत की सफलताओं पर निर्भर रहना – To rely on past achievements instead of striving for new success.
Example: "If you keep looking to your laurels, others will surpass you in the competition."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "stab someone in the back" is "to betray someone secretly" because it directly matches the context of Reginald betraying his closest friend. The other idioms are unrelated to betrayal.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To call in question
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: Challenge
Take a resolute stand
Show indifference
Dislike the arrangement
solution:
The correct answer is: Challenge

Explanation:
"To call in question" - "प्रश्न उठाना"
This idiom means to doubt or challenge the validity or truth of something. The correct option, "Challenge," fits best as it directly relates to questioning or disputing a statement, decision, or belief.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from legal and formal debates where raising doubts about a claim or argument was referred to as "calling it in question." Over time, it became a common expression for expressing skepticism or opposition.

Example:
"The lawyer called the witness's testimony in question during the trial."
"वकील ने मुकदमे के दौरान गवाह के बयान पर प्रश्न उठाया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "To call in question" is "Challenge" because it signifies raising doubts or objections. The other options—"Take a resolute stand," "Show indifference," and "Dislike the arrangement"—do not align with the idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Off and on
(Combined Higher Secondary Level Exam 2020)
options: every day
not soon
sometimes but not regularly
again and again
solution:
The correct answer is: sometimes but not regularly

Explanation:
"Off and on" - "कभी-कभी, अनियमित रूप से"
This idiom means something that happens occasionally or intermittently, not on a fixed schedule. The correct option "sometimes but not regularly" perfectly captures this meaning.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase "off and on" likely comes from the idea of switching between two states—being "on" (active/happening) and "off" (inactive/not happening). Over time, it evolved to describe sporadic occurrences.

Example:
"He works on his novel off and on, whenever he finds time."
"वह अपने उपन्यास पर कभी-कभी काम करता है, जब भी उसे समय मिलता है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "off and on" is "sometimes but not regularly" because it describes irregular or occasional occurrences. The other options ("every day," "not soon," "again and again") do not match the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
Over and above

(CHSL Exam 2022 Tier I)
options: To sum up the conversation
In addition to
Above all
Highest rank
solution:
The correct answer is: In addition to

Explanation:
"Over and above" - "इसके अलावा / इसके ऊपर भी"
The phrase "over and above" means something extra or in addition to what is already present or expected. The best fit among the options is "In addition to," which conveys the same meaning.

Origin of the Idiom:
The idiom "over and above" originates from Middle English, where "over" and "above" were used together to emphasize excess or surplus. It has been in use since the 15th century to indicate something beyond the usual or required amount.

Example:
"She received a bonus over and above her regular salary."
"उसे नियमित वेतन के अलावा एक बोनस भी मिला।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Over and above" is "In addition to" because it signifies something extra beyond what is already present. The other options do not convey the same sense of addition or surplus.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Bet one’s boots
(CT Non GD)
options: To be sure or certain
To get involved in a fight
To ignore someone
To do nothing or being inactive
solution:
The correct answer is: To be sure or certain

Explanation:
"Bet one’s boots" - "पूरी तरह से निश्चित होना"
This idiom means to be completely confident or certain about something, so much so that one is willing to bet their valuable possessions (like boots) on it.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the American Old West, where boots were an essential and valuable part of a person's attire. Betting one’s boots symbolized extreme confidence in an outcome, as losing them would be a significant sacrifice.

Example:
"I’d bet my boots that she’ll win the competition—she’s the best performer."
"मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि वह प्रतियोगिता जीतेगी—वह सबसे अच्छी प्रदर्शन करने वाली है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Bet one’s boots" is "To be sure or certain" because it conveys absolute confidence in a statement or prediction. The other options do not relate to the idiom's meaning of certainty.

question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Back to back
(SICPO Paper I 2024)
options: Try to get something.
Something follows immediately after something else.
Do something very fast or with great energy.
Present and discuss the details of something.
solution:
The correct answer is: Something follows immediately after something else.

Explanation:
"Back to back" - "एक के बाद एक तुरंत"
This idiom means that two or more events or actions occur consecutively without any gap in between.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the literal sense of two objects or people standing with their backs touching each other, symbolizing close succession. Over time, it evolved to describe events happening one after another without interruption.

Example:
"The team played two back-to-back matches in a single day."
"टीम ने एक ही दिन में लगातार दो मैच खेले।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "back to back" is "Something follows immediately after something else." because it denotes consecutive occurrences without delay. The other options do not relate to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Get your act together
(MTS Non Tech Havaldar CBIC and CBN Examination 2023)
options: To stay together
Get organised and do things better
To have patience
To act in a play
solution:
The correct answer is: Get organised and do things better

Explanation:
"Get your act together" - "अपने काम को सुव्यवस्थित करो और बेहतर तरीके से करो"
This idiom means to improve your behavior, work, or performance by becoming more organized and efficient. It implies taking control of a situation and making necessary changes to succeed.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the world of theater, where actors must rehearse and coordinate their performances ("act") properly to put on a good show. Over time, it evolved into a general expression urging someone to improve their efforts.

Example:
"If you want to pass the exam, you need to get your act together and start studying seriously."
"अगर तुम परीक्षा में पास होना चाहते हो, तो तुम्हें अपने काम को सुव्यवस्थित करना होगा और गंभीरता से पढ़ाई शुरू करनी होगी।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Get your act together" is "Get organised and do things better" because it conveys the idea of improving efficiency and discipline. The other options ("To stay together," "To have patience," "To act in a play") are unrelated to this idiom's meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
I just went to Bali on a backpacking trip and did everything by the ear without any itinerary.
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: by improvisation
by spreading rumors
by asking
while criticising
solution:
The correct answer is: by improvisation

Explanation:
"by the ear" - "बिना योजना के, तात्कालिक तरीके से"
The idiom "by the ear" means doing something spontaneously without prior planning, relying on instinct or immediate decisions rather than a fixed plan.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from music, where playing "by ear" means performing without reading sheet music, relying instead on listening and intuition. Over time, it has been extended to mean acting without a structured plan.

Example:
"Since we didn’t have a guidebook, we explored the city by the ear."
"चूंकि हमारे पास गाइडबुक नहीं थी, हमने शहर को बिना योजना के घूमा।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "by the ear" is "without prior planning, spontaneously" because it aligns with making decisions on the spot rather than following a set itinerary. The other options—spreading rumors, asking, or criticizing—are unrelated to the idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the sentence given below.

Richa was provoking her neighbours against her maid Shanta who spoke against her but none of them responded.
(CHSL Exam 2023 Tier I)
options: Egging on
Carrying the conviction
Rising like a phoenix
Smelling a rat
solution:
The correct answer is: Egging on

Explanation:
The phrase "provoking her neighbours" suggests that Richa was encouraging or urging them to act against her maid. The idiom "egging on" means to encourage someone to do something, often something negative or risky, which fits perfectly in this context.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

Egging on – उकसाना / भड़काना – To urge or encourage someone to do something, often something unwise.
Example: "The crowd egged on the fighters instead of stopping them."

Carrying the conviction – विश्वास जगाना – To strongly persuade someone of the truth or validity of something.
Example: "His speech carried the conviction that change was necessary."

Rising like a phoenix – फीनिक्स की तरह उठना – To make a strong comeback after a failure or downfall.
Example: "After bankruptcy, he rose like a phoenix and rebuilt his business."

Smelling a rat – कुछ संदेह होना – To suspect that something is wrong or dishonest.
Example: "When he avoided eye contact, I smelled a rat."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Egging on" is "encouraging someone to do something, often negative" because it matches the context of Richa provoking her neighbours. The other idioms do not fit the situation.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Lily-livered
(Combined Graduate Level Examination Tier I 2023)
options: Not brave
Comical
Naughty
Brave
solution:
The correct answer is: Not brave

Explanation:
"Lily-livered" - "डरपोक या कायर"
The idiom "lily-livered" refers to someone who lacks courage or is easily frightened. The term "liver" was historically believed to be the seat of emotions, and a "white" or "lily-colored" liver was thought to indicate cowardice.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from medieval physiology, where the liver was considered the source of passion and bravery. A pale or white liver (lily-livered) was believed to signify a lack of blood and, consequently, a lack of courage.

Example:
"He was too lily-livered to stand up to the bully."
"वह बदमाश के सामने खड़े होने में बहुत डरपोक था।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "lily-livered" is "not brave" because it directly refers to cowardice. The other options—comical, naughty, or brave—do not align with the idiom's historical and contextual meaning.

question:

Level playing field

(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: Avoiding differences
A fair competition
Lack of intelligence
Forgetting conflicts
solution:

"Level playing field" - "एक निष्पक्ष प्रतिस्पर्धा"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Level playing field" is "A fair competition" because it signifies equal opportunity for all participants. The other options do not relate to the idiom's true meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Where the shoe pinches
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: Where the comfort is more
Tight fitting shoes
Expensive shoes
Where the difficulty lies
solution:
The correct answer is: Where the difficulty lies

Explanation:
"Where the shoe pinches" - "जहाँ परेशानी होती है"
This idiom refers to the exact point or situation where a problem or difficulty arises. Just as a tight shoe causes discomfort in a specific spot, the phrase metaphorically indicates the source of trouble or hardship.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase originates from the literal discomfort caused by ill-fitting shoes. Over time, it evolved into a metaphorical expression highlighting the specific area of difficulty in any situation.

Example:
"He earns well, but with so many loans, that's where the shoe pinches."
"वह अच्छी कमाई करता है, लेकिन इतने कर्ज़ों के कारण, यही वह जगह है जहाँ परेशानी होती है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Where the shoe pinches" is "Where the difficulty lies" because it accurately represents the source of trouble in a given situation. The other options describe literal shoe-related scenarios, which are unrelated to the idiom's figurative meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He flatters the boss to his face but criticises him in his absence.
(Head Constable Ministerial)
options: behind the scenes
at home
behind his back
at random
solution:
The correct answer is: behind his back

Explanation:
The phrase "in his absence" in the sentence implies that the person criticizes the boss when he is not present. The idiom "behind his back" perfectly fits this context, as it means to say or do something about someone when they are not aware of it, often in a negative or deceitful way.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

behind the scenes – पर्दे के पीछे – (Working or happening privately, not seen by the public)
Example: "The negotiations were happening behind the scenes, away from the media."

at home – घर पर – (Physically present in one's house)
Example: "She prefers to work at home rather than in the office."

behind his back – उसकी पीठ पीछे – (Doing or saying something about someone without their knowledge, often negatively)
Example: "He pretends to be nice to her but gossips behind her back."

at random – बिना सोचे-समझे – (Without any specific order or pattern)
Example: "The winner was chosen at random from all the entries."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "behind his back" is "doing something secretly or deceitfully when someone is not present" because it accurately describes criticizing someone in their absence. The other options do not fit the context of the sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
By hook or by crook
(Junior Engineer (Civil))
options: In all directions
By virtue of
By any means
On the whole
solution:
The correct answer is: By any means

Explanation:
"By hook or by crook" - "किसी भी तरह से"
This idiom means achieving something using any possible method, whether fair or unfair. The correct option, "By any means," aligns perfectly with this meaning as it implies doing whatever is necessary to accomplish a goal.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from medieval England, where peasants were allowed to gather firewood from forests using only a hook (a tool) or a crook (a shepherd's staff). Over time, it evolved to signify achieving something by any method available.

Example:
"He was determined to win the competition by hook or by crook."
"वह प्रतियोगिता जीतने के लिए किसी भी तरह से दृढ़संकल्प था।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "By hook or by crook" is "By any means" because it conveys the idea of achieving a goal through any possible method. The other options do not relate to this idiom's intended meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.Spill the beans
(Constable GD Examination 2025)
options: To drop something accidentally
To clean up a mess
To tell people secret information
To cook a meal
solution:
The correct answer is: To tell people secret information

Explanation:
"Spill the beans" - "राज़ खोल देना"
This idiom means to reveal secret or confidential information, often unintentionally. It fits the context of disclosing something that was meant to be kept hidden.

Origin of the Idiom:
The exact origin is unclear, but one theory suggests it comes from ancient Greek voting practices where beans were used to cast secret ballots. If someone "spilled the beans," they accidentally revealed the votes. Another theory links it to the idea of spilling a container of beans, exposing what was inside.

Example:
"She spilled the beans about the surprise party."
"उसने सरप्राइज पार्टी के बारे में राज़ खोल दिया।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Spill the beans" is "To tell people secret information" because it refers to revealing confidential details. The other options are unrelated to the idiom's actual meaning.

question:
Select the appropriate meaning of the idiom “the heel of Achilles”
(Clerk)
options: A weak point
Failure in something
A man with perfect physique
To go to the war
solution:
The correct answer is: A weak point

Explanation:
"The heel of Achilles" - "एक कमजोर बिंदु"
This idiom refers to a vulnerable or weak spot in an otherwise strong person or thing. It originates from Greek mythology, where Achilles was invulnerable except for his heel, which became his fatal weakness.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase comes from the legend of Achilles, a Greek hero of the Trojan War. His mother, Thetis, dipped him in the River Styx to make him invincible, but she held him by his heel, leaving it unprotected. He was later killed by an arrow to his heel, making "Achilles' heel" a metaphor for a critical weakness.

Example:
"Despite his intelligence, his lack of confidence is his Achilles' heel."
"अपनी बुद्धिमत्ता के बावजूद, आत्मविश्वास की कमी उसका एक कमजोर बिंदु है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "the heel of Achilles" is "a weak point" because it signifies a single vulnerability in an otherwise strong entity. The other options do not align with the idiom's historical and metaphorical meaning.

question:
Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined phrase in the following sentence.

It was a great chance. You missed out an opportunity.
(Constable GD Examination 2022)
options: are dead as a dodo
are a blessing in disguise
are in the middle of nowhere
missed the boat
solution:
The correct answer is: missed the boat 

Explanation:
The phrase "missed out an opportunity" means failing to take advantage of a favorable chance. The idiom "missed the boat" perfectly fits this context as it means to lose an opportunity by being too slow or late to act.

Let's Explain All IDIOMS & Their Meanings:

"are dead as a dodo" – बिल्कुल मर चुका – (Completely extinct or obsolete)
Example: "Floppy disks are dead as a dodo now."

"are a blessing in disguise" – छिपा हुआ वरदान – (Something bad that turns out to be good)
Example: "Losing that job was a blessing in disguise because I found a better one."

"are in the middle of nowhere" – सुनसान जगह पर – (In a remote or isolated place)
Example: "Their car broke down in the middle of nowhere."

"missed the boat" – मौका गँवा देना – (To miss an opportunity by delay or inaction)
Example: "He missed the boat by not investing in Bitcoin early."

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "missed the boat" is "to lose an opportunity" because it directly matches the idea of failing to take advantage of a good chance. The other idioms are unrelated to the context of missing an opportunity.

question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Have your head in the clouds
(SICPO Paper I 2024)
options: The pilot had his head in the clouds while flying a plane.
She had her head in the clouds by wearing a cloud-shaped hat.
He had his head in the clouds during an important meeting.
They had their heads in the clouds by looking up at the sky during a meteor shower.
solution:
The correct answer is: He had his head in the clouds during an important meeting.

Explanation:
"Have your head in the clouds" - "ख्यालों में खोए रहना"
This idiom means to be daydreaming or not paying attention to reality. The correct option fits because it describes someone being distracted or lost in thought during a serious situation (an important meeting).

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase likely originates from the imagery of someone’s thoughts being so lofty or distracted that they seem to be floating among the clouds, disconnected from the real world.

Example:
"She always has her head in the clouds instead of focusing on her studies."
"वह हमेशा पढ़ाई पर ध्यान देने की बजाय ख्यालों में खोई रहती है।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "He had his head in the clouds during an important meeting." is "being distracted or lost in thought" because it shows the person was not mentally present in a crucial situation. The other options either take the idiom literally or misuse its figurative meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hit the sack
(CHSL 2021 Tier I)
options: Complete the assignment
Go to sleep
Miss  the mark
Confirm the target
solution:
The correct answer is: Go to sleep

Explanation:
"Hit the sack" - "सोने जाना"
This idiom means to go to bed or go to sleep. It is a casual and informal way of saying that someone is going to rest.

Origin of the Idiom:
The phrase "hit the sack" dates back to the early 20th century when mattresses were often stuffed with sacks of hay or cloth. "Hitting the sack" literally meant lying down on the bed. Over time, it became a common expression for going to sleep.

Example:
"I'm exhausted after work; I'm going to hit the sack early tonight."
"काम के बाद मैं बहुत थक गया हूँ; आज रात मैं जल्दी सोने जा रहा हूँ।"

Conclusion:
The correct meaning of "Hit the sack" is "Go to sleep" because it directly refers to the act of going to bed. The other options are unrelated to this idiom's meaning.
